### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, touching **5** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via MarketplaceInstallLocalPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **7** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 162fe54fbbd14d3415a4d72e13abd9a610eedcaf` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d2ee379fe70d618b2575ffe62913fd86064d1f94` — the merge of head `f54ec13b444d4a671865a641dbbe8d07896fb686` into base `162fe54fbbd14d3415a4d72e13abd9a610eedcaf`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d2ee379fe70d618b2575ffe62913fd86064d1f94 && git checkout d2ee379fe70d618b2575ffe62913fd86064d1f94
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 162fe54fbbd14d3415a4d72e13abd9a610eedcaf f54ec13b444d4a671865a641dbbe8d07896fb686 && git checkout -B drift-repro 162fe54fbbd14d3415a4d72e13abd9a610eedcaf && git merge --no-ff f54ec13b444d4a671865a641dbbe8d07896fb686

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 162fe54fbbd14d3415a4d72e13abd9a610eedcaf
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 162fe54fbbd14d3415a4d72e13abd9a610eedcaf` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对 · ACCEPT (L1, first read) · Head-sha: f54ec13b444d4a671865a641dbbe8d07896fb686 · 2026-11-16T13:49Z

L1 thread L1-a for area o1-B, on the final head declared in 6918245890. I read card #34336, the scope note 6917833544, dev report 6917684209, and the full diff against merge base `719b6b53` (4 commits, 3 files, +363/−18). No L2 is owed: `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, and the PR is not governed.

- **Card relation.** The PR body says `Fixes #34336`. Card ask 1 (install and reseed read every package body, in package order) is built here. Ask 2 (an upgrade replays new seed keys into existing organizations) is not built here; it moved to #34405 and #34406 by scope note 6917833544. Same-family findings are on #34407. So `Fixes` closes the card on ask 1 with ask 2 carried elsewhere. The area should confirm that the card's done condition reads that way, or say so on the card when it closes.
- **One reader.** `seedDatasetsOf(body)` = `resolveStackCollection(body, 'data')` from `@objectstack/core` (`stack-collections.ts`), filtered to entries that have an `object` and `records`.
  - The top-level `data` wins whenever it is present, so a flat bundle, or a composed artifact that still carries the flattened union, is read once and never again per package. Otherwise each package body is read in `packages[]` order.
  - On this head, `git grep` in `marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts` finds no `manifest.data` / `converted.data` read left.
  - Every door goes through `seedDatasetsOf`: install, reseed and upgrade (`applySideEffects`), the rehydrate share and heal (`maybeHealSampleData`), purge, the sample-data count, and the listing's `withSampleData`.
- **Pins.** The new test file `marketplace-install-local-composed-bundle-seeds.test.ts` pins:
  - install, with core seeded before the module that depends on it and the datasets shared for new organizations;
  - reseed;
  - an upgrade that adds a package;
  - count and purge;
  - the listing;
  - a restart, both sharing and healing.

  Its three controls are: a flat bundle unchanged, a composed artifact with a flattened `data` read once, and a composed artifact with no datasets still answering `no-datasets`. Per 6917684209 the file was red on base (6 failed, controls green) and is 9/9 at head.
- **Changeset.** `patch` on `@objectstack/cloud-connection`. Each door it names matches a call site above.
  - The upgrade paragraph ("seeds the incoming version's datasets into the organization the request acts in … other organizations are not reseeded") states the flat-bundle behaviour, unchanged, and that matches the code.
  - It does not promise ask 2.
- **Checks on this head** (check-runs): 51 names, 35 success, 16 skipped (path-filtered, opt-in and queue-only), 0 failed, 0 pending.
- **Base.** PRBASE = `162fe54f` (Test Core plan, `Affected-set diff base`), so K = 4 to `origin/main`, below 15. Nothing since touches `cloud-connection/**` or `stack-collections.ts`. The planned merge of `origin/main` after p0 #34397 comes back to me as a merge-only delta.

### Should (not blocking)

- **The purge and count doors do not catch the reader's refusal.** `seedDatasetsOf` can now throw: `stackPackageBodies` raises the ADR-0112 refusal for a malformed `packages`. Three doors catch it and say why: the heal (warn, then skip), the listing (warn, then `withSampleData: false`) and `applySideEffects` (`seed-datasets-unread` in the summary). But `handlePurge` (`seedDatasetsOf(entry.manifest)`, around line 6068) and `handleSampleDataCount` (around line 6369) call it bare, so a ledger body with a malformed `packages` reaches the route's error path instead of an answer that names the entry.
  - It is not reachable through install, because the `manifest` service refuses those bytes first. Only a hand-edited or older ledger body could carry them.
  - Either route both doors through the same reason the reseed gives for an unreadable entry (`unreadableLedgerEntry`), with a pin, or record it in `## Acceptance notes` as accepted.

Landing: not Tier H. After the merge-only delta (if it comes) is read, area o1-B lands it.
